title: The Missing Three Meters
mechanism: Floor-plan arithmetic: a 12 m outside length versus 5 m + 4 m of rooms leaves a 3 m hidden room; only the architect of the wall could know.
q: Who knew about the hidden room?

seg.hook: A diamond vanished from a locked room. And the answer is three missing meters.
seg.case: Fenn House, midnight. The diamond vanishes from the study. One door, watched all night. Barred windows. The plan says the house is twelve meters long. The study is five. The library is four.
seg.s1: Ada, the cook: "I never leave the kitchen. I cook, I don't climb stairs."
seg.s2: Boris, the guard: "I watched that door all night. Well, I dozed off once, at three."
seg.s3: Cleo, the architect: "I designed the library wall myself, last spring. I was asleep at home."
seg.challenge: Twelve meters outside. Nine inside. Who knew about the hidden room? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Cleo. Twelve minus nine leaves three meters of hidden room. The thief never needed the door. Boris dozing was a false lead. Only the architect who built that wall knew the room existed.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Mislabeled Bags
mechanism: Classic mislabel logic: when every label is wrong, the bag labeled MIXED must be pure, so one draw from it identifies all three bags.

seg.hook: Every label is wrong. And one pick tells you everything.
seg.case: A smuggler switched the labels on three evidence bags. Coins, beads, or a mix. Every single label is wrong. You may take one item out of one bag.
seg.s1: Rina holds the bag labeled COINS.
seg.s2: Sol holds the bag labeled BEADS.
seg.s3: Teo holds the bag labeled MIXED.
seg.challenge: Whose bag do you open? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: Open Teo's bag. The label says mixed, but every label is wrong, so that bag holds only one kind. Say a coin comes out. Then Sol's bag, labeled beads, can't be beads or coins, so it's the mix. Rina's is beads.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Bitten Apple
mechanism: Dental signature: a bite mark with a missing top front tooth matches the one suspect with that gap; muddy boots are a false lead.

seg.hook: The thief left one clue they could not resist biting.
seg.case: A farmhouse pantry is robbed overnight. On the table lies a half-eaten apple. The bite is clear: in the top row, one front tooth is missing. Muddy boot prints lead to the door.
seg.s1: Dax, the farmhand, grins: "I was in the barn." Every tooth is there.
seg.s2: Milo, the neighbor: "My boots are muddy because I walk the fields." His smile is complete.
seg.s3: Lena, the cook, smiles: "I was asleep at home." A front tooth is missing.
seg.challenge: Who took the bite? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Lena. Teeth leave a signature. The bite has a gap where one top front tooth should be. Dax and Milo both have complete smiles. Milo's muddy boots were only a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Euro Before Its Time
mechanism: Anachronism: a letter dated 1998 mentions euros, but euro banknotes and coins only existed from 2002 (pesetas in Spain in 1998).

seg.hook: A dead man's loan letter. And one word that did not exist yet.
seg.case: Old Garza dies, and his farm is up for grabs. Three neighbors each show a loan letter signed by Garza, dated May nineteen ninety-eight. Each one says: the farm is mine, as repayment.
seg.s1: Dov's letter, yellowed with age: "I lend you five hundred thousand pesetas."
seg.s2: Elsa's letter, crisp and white: "I lend you five hundred thousand pesetas."
seg.s3: Finn's letter, yellowed with age: "I lend you five thousand euros."
seg.challenge: One letter is a fake. Who forged it? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Finn. In nineteen ninety-eight, Spain used pesetas. Euro notes and coins did not exist until two thousand two. Elsa's fresh paper was only a false lead. Finn aged his paper, but he forgot his money.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Blood Type Heir
mechanism: Blood-group genetics: two type O parents can only have a type O child, so only the type O claimant can be the heir.

seg.hook: Two parents. Three claimants. And the answer is in a drop of blood.
seg.case: Lord and Lady Ashby lost their only baby thirty years ago. Now three people claim to be the missing heir. The doctor checks the records. Lord Ashby, blood type O. Lady Ashby, blood type O.
seg.s1: Wade has Lord Ashby's famous chin. His blood type: A.
seg.s2: Zoe has Lady Ashby's green eyes. Her blood type: B.
seg.s3: Alec looks like neither of them. His blood type: O.
seg.challenge: Who is the real heir? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Alec. Two type O parents can only have a type O child. Wade's A and Zoe's B are impossible. The chin and the eyes were false leads. The proof was in the blood.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Impossible Month
mechanism: Date-format dialect: 7/18 only parses month-first (US convention); day-first writers (Spain, UK) could never write month 18.

seg.hook: A single date on a note gives the writer away. Look at the numbers.
seg.case: A threatening note is found at the bank. It is signed and dated: seven slash eighteen. Three clerks have worked there for years. One of them wrote it.
seg.s1: Ana grew up in Madrid. She says she never saw the note.
seg.s2: Ben grew up in Boston. He says he was at lunch.
seg.s3: Cai grew up in London. He says he was on the phone.
seg.challenge: Who wrote the note? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Ben. In Madrid and London, the day comes first. Seven slash eighteen would be month eighteen, which does not exist. Only in America do people write the month first. Ben forgot where he learned to write.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Honest Odometer
mechanism: Round-trip odometer arithmetic: an 80 km logged trip equals twice the 40 km to the shop, contradicting a 5 km dentist claim.

seg.hook: The odometer never lies. Only the driver does.
seg.case: A jewelry shop forty kilometers from town is robbed at noon. Three coworkers each borrowed the same company car that afternoon. Every trip is logged on the odometer.
seg.s1: Pete drove to the gym, five kilometers away. The odometer went up ten.
seg.s2: Lucy drove to the airport, twenty-five kilometers away. The odometer went up fifty.
seg.s3: Omar drove to the dentist, five kilometers away. The odometer went up eighty.
seg.challenge: Who drove to the shop? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Omar. A round trip doubles the distance. Pete's ten and Lucy's fifty match their stories. Eighty is exactly twice the forty kilometers to the shop. Omar's dentist was a lie.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Crooked E
mechanism: Typewriter fingerprint: only one machine reproduces both flaws of the note (raised E and broken T); each other machine matches only one.
board: EVERY T HAS A BROKEN BAR

seg.hook: Every typewriter has a signature. This note has two flaws.
seg.case: A man gets a threat typed on plain paper, and is found dead the next day. In the note, every letter E sits a little too high. And every letter T has a broken top bar. The detective tests each suspect's machine.
seg.s1: Vera bought the same paper that day. Her machine's E sits too high. Her T is perfect.
seg.s2: Walt threatened the victim in public. His machine's T has a broken bar. His E is perfect.
seg.s3: Yara has no known motive. On her machine, the E sits too high, and the T has a broken bar.
seg.challenge: Who typed the threat? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Yara. A typewriter leaves flaws like a fingerprint. Only her machine matches both the high E and the broken T. Vera matched one flaw, Walt the other. Neither was enough.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Allergic Alibi
mechanism: Allergy cannot be faked: a severely cat-allergic man claiming an evening with six cats shows no symptoms, so he was never there.
q: Who is lying about the evening?

seg.hook: His body told the truth. His alibi did not.
seg.case: Mr. Voss is found dead at nine. Three alibis. One of them hides a detail that nobody can fake: a sneeze.
seg.s1: Lars: "I spent the evening with my sister's six cats." But Lars is severely allergic to cats. Yet his eyes are clear, and he took no medicine.
seg.s2: Mina: "I was in the greenhouse, among the lilies." She has no allergies.
seg.s3: Noor: "I was in the stables, with the horses." She has no allergies.
seg.challenge: Who is lying about the evening? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Lars. A cat allergy cannot be hidden. An evening with six cats means sneezing, red eyes, and a swollen nose. Lars has none of it. He was never there. Mina and Noor have nothing to hide.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Name in the Crowd
mechanism: Reflex to one's own name: shouting a fugitive's real name makes only the fugitive turn, even briefly; packed suitcase and nerves are false leads.

seg.hook: A fugitive can change his name. But not what his brain does when he hears it.
seg.case: A wanted man, Edmund Crane, hides in a boarding house under a false name. Three new lodgers. At dinner, the detective calls out from the back of the room: Edmund!
seg.s1: Kit has a packed suitcase by the door. When the name rings out, he keeps stirring his tea.
seg.s2: Leon says he is a retired teacher. When the name rings out, his head turns for half a second.
seg.s3: Mara is nervous, and stares at the exit. When the name rings out, she keeps staring.
seg.challenge: Who is Edmund Crane? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Leon. We react to our own name before we can think, even a man who has hidden it for years. Kit's suitcase and Mara's nerves were false leads. Only Leon turned.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Sun Lens
mechanism: Burning-glass optics: a round water-filled glass vase on a sunny sill focuses 2 PM sunlight into a fire on the desk with nobody present.

seg.hook: A fire started in an empty, locked room. And nobody lit a match.
seg.case: At two in the afternoon, a fire starts on a desk in a locked study. Everyone was away. No match, no wires. Just one burn mark, in the path of the sun. On the sill sits a round glass vase of water, new since yesterday.
seg.s1: Orla, the maid: "I open those curtains every single morning."
seg.s2: Piers, the florist: "I delivered roses at nine, in a round glass vase, on the sill. The order said a wooden box."
seg.s3: Reed, the secretary: "I locked the study at ten and went to lunch."
seg.challenge: Who set the fire? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Piers. A round vase of water works like a magnifying glass. At two, the sun focuses through it onto the desk. Orla's curtains were a false lead. They open every day. The new vase was the difference.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Warm Bulb
mechanism: Heat memory of an incandescent bulb: on-then-off leaves it warm and dark; currently on is lit; never touched is cold.
tags: on for ten minutes, then off

seg.hook: Three switches. One bulb. One visit. And the answer is hiding in the heat.
seg.case: A vault has three switches in the hall, and one bulb inside. You can enter the vault only once. Sal runs the first switch, Tia runs the second, Uri runs the third.
seg.s1: Sal's switch is left on for ten minutes, then turned off.
seg.s2: Tia's switch is turned on, and left on.
seg.challenge: You step inside. The bulb is dark, but warm. Whose switch controls the light? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Sal. A bulb that burned for ten minutes grows hot, and stays warm after it goes dark. If it were Tia's, it would shine. If it were Uri's, it would be cold. Warm and dark means Sal's switch.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.
